subject: ing
title: Spanish verb times: one word or two?

points.heading: One-word verb times
points.body:
Central idea: A verb tells an action. A simple tense uses one Spanish verb word to show when an action happens.

Explore: The indicative is used for facts. Compare: «canto» means I sing now; «cantaba» tells about a repeated or ongoing past; «canté» tells a finished past action.

Practice: Write five forms of cantar: canto, cantaba, canté, cantaré, cantaría. Say when each action happens.

Common mistake: Do not use cantaba for one finished action yesterday; use canté for that kind of story.

points.heading: Two-word verb times
points.body:
Central idea: A compound tense uses two words: a form of haber plus a participle.

Explore: A participle is an already-finished form, such as cantado or comido. In «he cantado», he is the helper and cantado is the participle.

Practice: Circle the helper in he cantado and underline cantado. Then write había cantado and habré cantado.

Common mistake: Do not make the participle plural: write hemos comido, not hemos comidos.

points.heading: Choose the form that tells your story
points.body:
Central idea: Choose a verb form by thinking about the time and meaning of the action.

Explore: Use «terminé ayer» for a finished yesterday action. Use «he terminado» when the finished action matters now.

Practice: Write one sentence with a one-word form and one with a two-word form. Tell what changed.

Common mistake: Do not choose a form only because it is longer. Choose the form that matches the story.

lesson.summary: This lesson teaches spanish verb times: one word or two. Understand the central idea first, then explore it, practice it, and check a common mistake.

questions.prompt: Which Spanish form shows an action happening now?
Which form tells about a finished action yesterday?

choices: A repeated or ongoing past action.
questions.answer: A repeated or ongoing past action.

questions.prompt: What two parts make a compound tense?
choices: A form of haber and a participle.
questions.answer: A form of haber and a participle.

questions.prompt: In «he cantado», which word is the participle?
Why should «comido» stay the same in «hemos comido»?
choices: It is always a future word.
The participle does not become plural for the subject.
questions.answer: The participle does not become plural for the subject.

questions.prompt: Which one-word Spanish form can mean «I sing»?
Which form fits a closed action in the past?

choices: A repeated or ongoing past action.
questions.answer: A repeated or ongoing past action.

questions.prompt: What do you need to build a two-word Spanish tense?
choices: A form of haber and a participle.
questions.answer: A form of haber and a participle.

questions.prompt: Which word names the finished-form part?
What is the rule for the participle in this example?
choices: The participle does not become plural for the subject.
It is always a future word.
questions.answer: The participle does not become plural for the subject.
